title: Choose Budgie's visual world
question: The roll assigned Security Print. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All options keep the deep green, warm grey, logo colours, logo and pixel budgie.

options.label: Security Print
options.lineage: Banknote and passbook security printing: guilloche, intaglio, microprint, watermark window
options.thesis: Budgie is engraved like something that holds value: the year's forecast drawn as a guilloche rosette.
options.viewport: Headline 'It sees December coming' on the left; on the right a 12-lobe guilloche rosette, one lobe per month of a sample forecast, with December swelling in orange and the pixel budgie in the watermark window. The early-access button sits under the headline.
options.risk: If the guilloche gets too literal it can read as imitating peso notes. It needs restraint: no denominations, seals or portraits.

raised.raise: Microprint is made of real data: the forecast figures themselves become the fine-line texture, never lorem.
One measured graticule: a 12-month ring and grid that every section aligns to, so the year is the page's ruler.
Colour lives only in the hairlines. Text stays in green ink, and the logo colours appear only as fine engraved lines.
Orange is reserved for the decisive beat: it marks only the costly months (December, enrollment, summer Meralco), never decoration.
Name the obvious plainly: section labels say what they are, like the denomination line on a note.

options.label: Kalendaryo
options.lineage: The free bakery and hardware-store wall calendar in every Filipino kitchen
options.thesis: The page is this year's wall calendar, already flipped to December, compliments of Budgie.
options.viewport: A huge DISYEMBRE calendar sheet hanging on the right with red holidays and a green 'Compliments of Budgie' sponsor band; the headline and CTA sit on the left.
options.risk: The most familiar direction here. It tends toward the kitschy-Pinoy look you ruled out, and it is less luxurious than asked.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each payday is a junction: yellow bands name the costly months ahead and how far away they are.
options.viewport: A giant yellow band reading 'December ahead. Plan now.' with a monumental 12, then bands for Enrollment, Meralco summer rates and Christmas with distance in months.
options.case: Strong on product clarity because it is one message per band. It loses on audience identification and on luxury.
options.risk: The yellow overwhelms the brand green, and it reads as transit rather than premium.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The forecast as a strobing black-and-white barcode field.
options.viewport: A wall of forecast bars with a sine curve tracing December.
options.case: Its black-and-white-only rule breaks the brand colours, and it reads cold and academic.
options.kept: Numbers as material: the microprint is real forecast data.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.thesis: Spending as a phosphor trace locked by a trigger.
options.viewport: A green trace on black glass.
options.case: Neon-on-black is the generic fintech gloss you ruled out, and it is a tool costume.
options.kept: One measured graticule that every section aligns to.

options.label: Industrial Quotes
options.case: Ironic and loud, the opposite of luxurious and trustworthy.
options.kept: Plain literal labels that name what each section is.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: Calm white field with spectral hairline edges.
options.viewport: A quiet white page with a mint-violet fringe.
options.case: Clean but placeless: nothing about it is Filipino or about money.
options.kept: Colour confined to hairlines while text stays in ink.

options.label: Screentone Page
options.viewport: Panels with a full-black December beat.
options.case: Too playful for money, and it drops the brand colours.
options.kept: Reserve the strongest colour for the decisive beat only.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished fintech landing page: warm grey, deep green, a phone mockup beside the headline, and feature rows.
canonCard.viewport: A split hero: headline and CTA on the left, an app screenshot in a phone frame on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other finance apps by design, and close to the current page.
